_instructions: Use these prompts with ElevenLabs Voice Design (no audio samples needed).
Go to: https://elevenlabs.io/app/voice-lab → Add a new voice → Voice Design
Paste the 'prompt' text, set preview text to the 'preview_line', click Generate.
ElevenLabs will generate 3 candidates — pick the best one, save it, copy the voice ID.
Paste each voice ID into characters.json.
Alternatively use Voice Cloning (higher quality) — see prepare_voices.py for that workflow.

ARTHUR.prompt: An eight-year-old American boy with a warm, slightly earnest voice. Friendly and curious tone, with just a hint of a nasal quality typical of children that age. Energetic but not over-the-top. Clear diction, moderate pace, sounds like a real kid rather than a cartoon caricature. Perfect audio quality, studio recorded.
ARTHUR.preview_line: Hey, has anyone seen my library book? I left it right here and now it's gone.

DW.prompt: A four-year-old American girl with a bright, precocious, and slightly bossy voice. Higher pitch than Arthur, dramatic and self-assured. She speaks with the confidence of someone who is absolutely certain she is right about everything. Clear and expressive, with natural childlike inflections. Perfect audio quality, studio recorded.
DW.preview_line: I TOLD you there was a monster in the basement. Nobody ever listens to me.

TIMMY.prompt: A four-year-old American boy, one of a pair of energetic twins. High-pitched, excitable, slightly impish voice. Enthusiastic and easily wound up. He speaks quickly when excited. Sounds very young, playful, and a little mischievous. Perfect audio quality, studio recorded.
TIMMY.preview_line: Did you say monster? I brought a flashlight! Let's go find it right now!

TOMMY.prompt: A four-year-old American boy, twin brother, very similar to Timmy but with a marginally lower pitch and slightly more deadpan delivery. Still excitable but a touch calmer, often echoing or finishing his brother's thoughts. Playful and impish. Perfect audio quality, studio recorded.
TOMMY.preview_line: I wasn't scared at all. That was just a practice scream to see if my lungs still worked.

NARRATOR.prompt: A warm, friendly adult American male with a rich, clear storytelling voice. Think PBS Kids narrator — inviting, measured pace, gentle authority, slightly theatrical without being over-the-top. The kind of voice that makes children want to lean in and listen. Calm, articulate, and reassuring. Perfect audio quality, studio recorded.
NARRATOR.preview_line: It was a perfectly ordinary Tuesday morning in Elwood City — which meant, of course, that something extraordinary was about to happen.
